Which nights are Muay Thai fights on Koh Samui? | Six nights a week in Chaweng: Phetchbuncha Stadium on Monday, Wednesday and Saturday, and Samui International Muay Thai Stadium on Tuesday, Friday and Sunday, both from about 21:00 to around midnight. Neither stadium fights on Thursday.
How much are Muay Thai tickets on Koh Samui? | 1,500 THB for a standard seat, 2,000 THB ringside and 2,500 THB VIP at both stadiums in 2026, plus a 3,000 THB VIP premium seat at Samui International. Samui International lists half price for children aged 6–10 and free entry under 6.
Is ringside worth it at a Samui Muay Thai night? | For most people, yes. For 500 THB more than a standard seat you sit next to the ring, hear every kick and avoid the hard benches further back. The view is similar from any ringside seat, so you don't need to arrive very early, but book ahead for Fridays and Saturdays in high season.
Can children attend Muay Thai fights on Samui? | Yes. Children are allowed at both stadiums, and Samui International lists half price for ages 6–10 and free entry under 6. Fights end around midnight and the music is loud, so bring ear defenders for small children and sit a few rows back rather than ringside.
What time do Muay Thai fights start and finish on Koh Samui? | Phetchbuncha starts at about 21:00; at Samui International gates open at 20:00 and the first fight is listed for 21:30. A card of about six to eight bouts runs for two to three hours and usually ends around midnight.
Should I buy Muay Thai tickets in advance on Samui? | For ringside and VIP seats on Friday and Saturday from mid-December to April, yes, because tour groups buy blocks of seats. Standard seats are usually available at the box office. Never buy from street touts, who sometimes sell the wrong night or stadium.
Are there Muay Thai fights on Thursday on Koh Samui? | No. Thursday is the only night with no regular fights at either Chaweng stadium. On Thursdays, Chaweng Walking Street by Chaweng Lake is the main evening attraction instead.
Can I take photos at a Muay Thai fight? | Phone photos and short videos for personal use are normal at both stadiums. Don't use flash towards the fighters or stand in front of other spectators, and ask the stadium before bringing professional camera equipment.
